transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Aurora Partnerships), Leah Osei (Aurora BD), Dr. Priya Kapoor (Aurora Solutions)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Intro between Redwood and Aurora GPU Systems to explore partner program and technical integration options. Discussed deployment models (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), security/compliance requirements (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs), and next steps around benchmarks and partner docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. quick round robin, i'm maya chen, redwood ae, with jordan patel our se.
[00:12] Carlos: hi maya, carlos here, partnerships at aurora. leah and priya with me. thanks for setting this up.
[00:17] Jordan: hey all, jordan, i run solutions for infra and perf at redwood. we'll keep this high level then dig into tech as needed.
[00:28] Leah: quick Q — are you focusing on reseller partnership or more of a reference integration?
[00:33] Maya: great question. we're open to both. primary goal is cloud/gpu vendor partnerships where aurora can offer redwood-ready stacks to customers and we can co-sell. also exploring dedicated and private deployment pilots.
[00:45] Priya: what does redwood require for a private deployment — network, k8s, etc?
[00:49] Jordan: for private we usually support two modes: a VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed infra, or full on-prem package. requirements are fairly standard — k8s or baremetal with container runtime, access to plugin KMS or HSM for keys, and a way to expose GPUs to the runtime. we can also ship an appliance image.
[01:08] Carlos: and in terms of compliance — SOC two, iso27001, and audit logging — any blockers?
[01:13] Maya: we have SOC 2 and ISO work in our security pack; we'll share the security slide deck. audit logs and KMS integration are supported; we do recommend vault or AWS KMS. note: some terms in the slides are auto-gen and might say SOC two when the deck renders, little transcription hiccup.
[01:30] Leah: good. pricing and resale margin — curious how partner pricing looks for dedicated capacity.
[01:36] Maya: we'll follow up with partner program pricing. short answer: dedicated reservations have discounts and partner margin, plus co-marketing credits for early pilots. i'll include details in the deck.
[01:45] Jordan: from tech side, customers usually care about latency vs cost tradeoffs — dedicated pools give predictable latency; hosted api is easiest to adopt. we also do quantization profiles and batching to reduce token cost.
[02:02] Priya: any constraints on model types? we have customers wanting to run Llama-family and some mix of open weights and checkpointed models.
[02:10] Jordan: we support common open models, and our runtime picks kernels per architecture. for certain models we'll recommend different quantizations; sometimes customers prefer a tuned vram-optimized q4 profile. also worth noting — kv cache behavior on long contexts can affect memory; we can share typical seq length guidance.
[02:28] Carlos: can we do a benchmark? like sample gen latency at 8k seq and 2k seq across your hosted vs a dedicated aurora pool?
[02:36] Jordan: absolutely. typical benchmark plan: we run a set of 10 workloads, 50 concurrent sessions, and measure p50/p95 latency, throughput, and cost per token. we'll propose a 2-week test window.
[02:49] Maya: we'll need aurora to provide regions you want tested, and access to a partner account or ephemeral credentials. we'll also share a spreadsheet template.
[02:58] Leah: about networking — some customers require private peering and no internet egress. how do you handle that?
[03:04] Jordan: for private deployments we can use direct connect or VPC peering. in on-prem cases we can air-gap and ship offline packages; some features (like model catalog auto-updates) require opt-in networking.
[03:16] Carlos: any known integration with aurora's provisioning APIs? we have an infra API to spin up nodes and attach GPUs.
[03:22] Jordan: we can integrate. we typically expose terraform modules and have an operator. if aurora has an infra API, we can map calls to our operator — that's something the se team would scope.
[03:33] Maya: can we talk about commercial motion? what are your go-to-market priorities?
[03:37] Carlos: co-sell with cloud customers and sell aurora as a preferred infra for ML platform customers. also pushing into telco infra where latency matters.
[03:46] Maya: great fit. we can pilot a customer in telco where low p99 is needed and demonstrate lower TCO with dedicated pools + quantization.
[03:57] Priya: security ask — do you provide per-tenant encryption keys? we need per-customer KMS isolation.
[04:03] Jordan: yes, we support per-tenant KMS keys; we integrate with KMS/HSM providers and permit key rotations, audit logs, and CKMS. small note — sometimes transcript tools call it KMS or H M S weirdly.
[04:18] Leah: competitors — we've seen lambda and paperspace offer managed endpoints; how is redwood different?
[04:24] Maya: our positioning is production-first: unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, private with tooling for rollouts, tracing, and token-level cost breakdowns. we focus on predictable inference economics, not just access.
[04:40] Carlos: what's the dev experience like for customers — SDKs, auth?
[04:44] Jordan: we have REST + SDKs, streaming, function/tool calling, and model catalog. auth is API keys or SSO for the control plane. RBAC and SAML for enterprise.
[04:55] Priya: what about model weights and IP — do we store customer fine-tuned weights?
[04:59] Maya: we can store them in customer-controlled buckets or in our private tenant stores depending on the deployment. for private/on-prem the customer owns the data. for hosted, we have encryption at rest and KMS controls.
[05:12] Leah: can you share a partner checklist so our sales engineers know what to ask customers?
[05:16] Maya: yes, we'll share a checklist + partner playbook link after the call.
[05:22] Jordan: technical note — for perf, we'd like to know typical batch sizes and sequence length distributions; that influences kernel selection.
[05:30] Carlos: we'll pull that from our telemetry and share.
[05:33] Maya: next step summary — we'll send partner deck, security slides, and a benchmark plan. jordan will follow up with a sample perf test and requirements. aurora to share infra API docs and telemetry.
[05:45] Leah: timeline — can we aim to start a pilot mid-april to late april?
[05:50] Maya: that's tight but doable. we'll try to kick off benching week of 2026-04-20.
[06:00] Carlos: any red flags from your side?
[06:03] Jordan: none yet; main risks are scheduling and access to representative workloads. also if we need air-gapped verification it adds time.
[06:11] Maya: i'll include action items in the deck email. thanks everyone.
[06:18] Priya: thanks, very helpful. we'll get telemetry to you by monday.
[06:22] Meeting end.
